newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel lawmakers visit PLO Jerusalem headquarters.
newsitem.headline: Israel lawmakers visit PLO Jerusalem headquarters.

text.p: A handful of lawmakers on an Israeli parliamentary committee visited Orient House, the PLO's Jerusalem headquarters, on Sunday in defiance of government policy.

The visit, the first by Israeli legislators, coincided with Israeli diplomatic efforts to persuade the fact-finding "troika" of the European Union foreign ministers not to hold talks with Palestinians at Orient House.
Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring said on Saturday it was vital the troika visit Israel in the near future and also hold talks with the PLO.
Knesset Interior Committee chairman Salah Tarif of the opposition Labour party organised the visit, hosted by Faisal al-Husseini, the top PLO official in Jerusalem.

"We came to visit Orient House to hear the problems of the residents of East Jerusalem," Tarif, a Druze Arab, told reporters. He said the visit was "very official" and that a majority of committee members had voted in favour of it.
Tarif was accompanied by other Labour legislators on the 15-member committee, but right-wing and religious members boycotted the visit.

Orient House, in Arab East Jerusalem, is a symbol of the PLO's nationalist aspirations and its desire to make the eastern part of the city, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, capital of a future Palestinian state.
Israel regards both halves of the city as its capital, a claim that has failed to win international recognition.

Israeli leaders have warned the PLO not to conduct any activity associated with Palestinian self-rule at Orient House, saying Israeli-PLO peace deals restrict such activities to autonomous parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Lawmaker Zeev Boyem of the ruling Likud party, protesting outside Orient House, said the problems of Arab residents of East Jerusalem should be addressed to the Jerusalem municipality and not PLO headquarters.
"An address like this (Orient House) is an address that divides Jerusalem and this, it seems, is the stance of the Labour party," Boyem told reporters.
The Palestinian Authority recently gave in to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's demand that it shut two Jerusalem offices as a precondition to progress in Israeli-PLO peace talks.
Right-wing demonstrators said the offices had not been shut and that Orient House was an affront to Israeli sovereignty.
"Those bunch of terrorists fooled my prime minister," said Benny Elon of the far-right Moledet party.
Tarif said Netanyahu's satisfaction with the closure of the offices removed any obstacles to an official parliamentary visit to Orient House.
He said that while it was government policy to oppose visits to Orient House by foreign diplomats, it had no authority to prevent elected Israelis from going to PLO headquarters.
A spokesman for Netanyahu declined immediate comment on the visit.
